title: O God, Whose Presence Glows in All
description: O God, Whose Presence Glows in All in Tonic Solfa to WINCHESTER NEW, doh is C: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: Nathaniel Langdon Frothingham wrote these words. They were printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion, compiled by Samuel Longfellow and Samuel Johnson (Boston, 1848), as hymn 23, “For Spiritual Influences”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Long Metre (8.8.8.8), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to WINCHESTER NEW; any other Long Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: O God, whose pre-sence glows in all With-in, a-round us, and a-bove! Thy word we bless, Thy name we call, Whose word is Truth, whose name is Love.

lines: O God, whose presence glows in all
Thy word we bless, Thy name we call,
Whose word is Truth, whose name is Love.
That truth be with the heart believed
Of all who seek this sacred place;
With power proclaimed, in peace received,
Our spirit's light, Thy spirit's grace.
That love its holy influence pour,
To keep us meek, and make us free;
And throw its binding blessing more
Round each with all, and all with Thee.
Send down its angel to our side;
Send in its calm upon the breast;
For we would know no other guide,
And we can need no other rest.

source: A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848)
licence: Public domain: Nathaniel Langdon Frothingham died in 1870.
credits: Words by Nathaniel Langdon Frothingham (1793–1870), public domain, as printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848); set to WINCHESTER NEW by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
